pageCache.text:
Oaks Science Experiments
Year 6 have been diligently cultivating mould as part of their Science topic this term. They chose variables such as temperature and moisture, with some choosing to saturate the bread in varying liquids such as water, milk and coffee. They then observed the change over time and even got to look under a microscope (whilst holding their breath!!) to see the mould more closely. They discovered many things, such as coffee accelerating the process, sourdough not moulding quickly and keeping bread in a boiler cupboard turns it to toast over time!

Requesting leave of absence from school during term time.
The law does not grant parents/carers an automatic right to take their child out of school during term time. You may consider that a holiday will be an educational family experience, but your child will still miss out on the teaching that their peers will receive, which is something that we all have a responsibility to avoid. Any absence from school will disrupt your child’s learning. We have a collective responsibility to ensure that Ide Hill meets statutory requirements and obligations to ensure that children attend school regularly.

On Tuesday, the whole school gathered to say thank you and farewell to Mrs Boiling. The children have received so much care from her over the years, and all classes helped to create her very own first aid box, filled with messages and keepsakes. Mrs Boiling was delighted to receive messages and gifts from children, staff and parents alike. The outpouring of love for her is testament to her love and dedication to the school.

A message from our Chair of Governors, Mrs Fletcher
I would like to say a huge well done to all parents, carers and to your children for the resilience, imagination, dedication and hard work which you are all displaying in these uncertain and fast moving times. It is heart warming to see photos of your children's work and creations, much of which is being achieved at home, being reproduced in the weekly newsletter. I am very much looking forward to seeing the results of the next lockdown challenge.
I would also like to take this opportunity to say, on behalf of all the governors, a huge thank you and well done to the incredibly dedicated, hardworking and flexible staff team. Under Mrs Hillman's leadership they are doing a magnificent job with the remote learning. As you can see from the recent parent questionnaire, there is huge support for how they are delivering the learning, together with recognition of the care they are taking to support the wellbeing of all families.
I wish them, and all of you, a restful and fun half term and that the weather will be kind - whether it allows snowman building or some sun on everyone's faces -and we hope that it will not be too long before the children will be back together in their classrooms.

pageCache.pageTitle: Ide Hill Primary School - Our Governors
pageCache.text:
Our Governors
The Governing Body of Ide Hill school comprises 14 people, 13 governors and a clerk. The Governing Body of any school has 3 main roles:
Although not involved in the day-to-day running of the school, governors support and challenge the headteacher and staff. There are various types of governor: foundation (as Ide Hill is Voluntary Aided school these are people appointed by the Diocese or Parochial Church Council), LA appointed, Headteacher, Staff appointed governor, Parent elected governors and associate governors. Please note, associate governors do not have voting rights. The full Governing Body meets termly but smaller sub-committees, namely the Curriculum Committee and Finance also meet in between, either termly or more often as required.
Chair of Governors and Chair of the Strategy Committee
We are delighted that Anne Fletcher has been re-appointed as our Bishop's nominee and Chair of Governors. Anne has served the school in many ways over the last 11 years as Chair, Deputy Chair and Foundation Governor. Anne is the Head of the Strategy Committee and TLC Committee. Anne is the designated Safeguarding Governor and has a special passion for the Early Years Foundation Stage, as Anne ran the Ide Hill Village Pre-School very successfully for many years.
Miss Alexander joined Ide Hill Primary School as Headteacher in April 2024. As Headteacher, she is automatically an ex-officio governor. Miss Alexander is responsible for the organisation, management and strategic direction of the school. As such, it is her responsibility to implement the school improvement plan, and to collaborate with governors to monitor standards across the school. Miss Alexander is also the Designated Safeguarding Lead at Ide Hill School.
Miss Johnson has been an integral part of Ide Hill Primary School since 2002. She was appointed Deputy Headteacher in October 2022 and Co-headteacher in April 2024. Jeanine leads music and Religious Education. Jeanine is a Designated Safeguarding Lead.
Foundation Governor appointed by the PCC. Deputy Chair of Governors
Sue was voted onto the governing body in April 2015. Having graduated from Nottingham University in 1996 with a degree in mathematics, she worked as a chartered accountant at PricewaterhouseCoopers for 13 years. Sue has two children who both attended the school and now enjoys being a stay-at-home mum. For the many years, Sue was the treasurer of the PTA and book-keeper for Ide Hill pre school. She also helps at the school on a regular basis. In her spare time, Sue enjoys cooking, crafts and travel.
Foundation Governor appointed by the PCC. Chair of the Teaching and Learning Committee
Following university Niall qualified as a history teacher and taught for two years before moving into journalism and senior national roles in the health services. In the 1980s he was Editor of Nursing Times after which he joined the BBC as its first substantive health correspondent moving on to become Social Affairs Editor, broadcasting on both radio and television news. He went on to become Chief Executive of the health think tank The King's Fund, Chief Executive and registrar of the General Medical Council, the statutory body which regulates doctors in the UK, and chief executive of the NHS Confederation. He was the non executive chair of East Kent Hospitals NHS Trust until 2023. Niall is an Honorary Fellow of the Institute of Education and was awarded a CBE in the Queen's Birthday Honours 2017 for services to patient safety.
Appointed by the Sundridge with Ide Hill parochial Church Council, Richard joined the governing body in October 2010 having moved to Ide Hill when he retired. On the Governing body, he is responsible for building development and involved in other school activities as a member of the Finance and Premises Committee. Prior to his retirement, Richard was a civil engineer and director for W S Atkins, managing projects and business activities in the UK and overseas. Since retirement, for the past 5 years, he has had a voluntary role with CAFOD (The Catholic Agency for Overseas Development) and co-ordinates the Schools Programme for the Archdiocese of Southwark. He is a Director of the Ide Hill Community Shop CIC and was the project manager for the building of the new shop in the village. He now acts as the financial director, company secretary and co-ordinates the volunteering.
Jenny brings to the role of parent governor a passion for supporting our local village school and ensuring every child receives the best possible educational experience. Jenny has been a parent over the last seven years, with two children currently attending the school. Jenny has nearly 20 years of experience in primary education, working as both a class teacher and senior leader (including the role of deputy headteacher). This background has given Jenny a deep understanding of the challenges and opportunities within schools, including curriculum development, staff support, safeguarding, and raising standards for all learners which will support the school in maintaining high expectations and helping the school to continually improve.
Much of Hayley's working life has been dedicated to enabling children to reach their potential. Her career as a teacher began in a small village Church of England school, much like Ide Hill. Several years on Hayley became a senior leader in a large primary school, qualifying as a Special Educational needs Coordinator (SENCo), leading on Inclusion as Assistant Headteacher, also being the Designated Safeguarding lead (DSL). For four years, Hayley held the voluntary position of Vice-Chair, on a Board of Trustees for a charity promoting the voice of parents who have children with SEND. Hayley currently holds a specialist advisory role, to reduce challenging behaviour across primary schools in a London Borough.
Foundation Governor appointed by the PCC
Barbara has been a resident in Ide Hill since October 2017. One of Barbara's sons lives in the village and the other is nearby in Chipstead. Barbara's working background was in education. Barbara trained as a teacher at Stockwell College of Education in Bromley and was appointed to Holy Cross RC Primary School in Catford where she worked until retirement in 2009.
Jane ran Ide Hill Pre-School in the in the late 1980s-1993 and was a nursery teacher at Granville School in Sevenoaks for over 15 years. She has lived in the local area for 45 years. Her three children and three stepchildren attended the school and during that time she was an active member of the PTA. Jane now has granddaughters at the school and is an active volunteer in our Year 2 class.
With 12 years experience in the education sector, Taricia currently serves as the fundraising manager for a residential special school, successfully raising funds for various projects, from iPads to multi-million-pound capital developments. Previously, as General Manager of a large secondary school, Taricia managed all soft facilities services and has experience in procedure development, policy writing, GDPR compliance, financial management and strategic planning.
Local Authority Governor
Paul qualified as a Chartered Accountant and worked at BP for more than 32 years in various senior financial roles. These included CFO of BP Greece, BP Europe Financial Controller and BP Group Finance Tax CFO. Since 2015 Paul has been largely retired and has enjoyed voluntary roles including at Caterham School in his role as Treasurer of the Old Caterhamian’s Association as well as a Member of the Caterham School Foundation. Paul is also Treasurer of the Friends of Limpsfield Common and volunteers half a day a week as a member of the Limpsfield Common Task force. Paul joins the Finance Committee at Ide Hill Primary School where he will use his skills and experience to oversee effective use of the schools resources.
Mrs. Farrar has been a teacher for 25 years and joined Ide Hill Primary school in 2013 as a Class Teacher. During that time Mrs. Farrar has taught in Years 6, 4, 3, 2 and 1. Mrs Farrar has been subject lead for a variety of subjects at Ide Hill including Art/DT, PHSE, writing and science. Mrs Farrar has two children and in her spare time enjoys spending time with her family, cooking and walking her dog. As staff governor Mrs. Farrar brings the staff's perspective to the governing body, acting as a link between staff and leadership, while participating in strategic decisions like vision, finance, and accountability, always serving the whole school's best interests.

Rachel joined Ide Hill Primary School as Bursar in 2012 and has clerked various committees throughout that time. Rachel become the Clerk to the Governing Body, including the Full Governing Body in January 2017. As Clerk, she is responsible for ensuring that all matters discussed within the governing body are documented and that it proceeds in an orderly and productive manner. She coordinates and prepares Governors’ meetings, as well as ensuring that policy documents are circulated and formally agreed.

Part 2: Cookie Policy
Cookies are small data files that are placed on your computer or mobile device when you visit a website. Cookies are widely used by online service providers in order to (for example) make their websites or services work, or to work more efficiently, as well as to provide reporting information.
Cookies set by the website owner or service provider (in this case, eSchools) are called “first party cookies”. Cookies set by parties other than the website owner are called “third party cookies”. Third party cookies enable third party features or functionality to be provided on or through the website or service you are using (such as advertising, interactive content and analytics). The third parties that set these third party cookies can recognise your computer both when it visits the website or service in question and also when it visits certain other websites or services.
We use first party and third party cookies for several reasons. Some cookies are required for technical reasons in order for our Services to operate, and we refer to these as “essential” cookies. Other cookies enable us and the third parties we work with to track and target the interests of visitors to our Services, and we refer to these as “advertising” or “analytical” cookies. For example, the embedding of YouTube and Vimeo videos, as added by individual schools, will require “advertising” cookies to be enabled in order to successfully play them. Schools that, for example, opt to track visitor data using Google Analytics will require “analytical” cookies to be enabled in order to do so. These third party cookies are used to tailor content and information that we may send or display to you and otherwise personalise your experience while interacting with our Services and to otherwise improve the functionality of the Services we provide. We also enable schools to employ cookies and similar tracking technologies in connection with their use of our Services in order to allow them to track visitors to and interactions with their school website.
eSchools websites may request cookies to be set on your device. We use cookies to let us know when you visit our websites, how you interact with us and to enrich your user experience. The cookies differ depending on the information. You can adapt your cookie preferences, although please note that blocking some types of cookies may impact your experience on our websites and the services we are able to offer. We will not, without your express consent, supply your personal information to any third party for the purpose of their or any other third party's direct marketing.
Our Services allows schools to embed code which may potentially contain cookies. Please note embedded content, if displayed on one of our websites, has been added by the school and not by eSchools. The embedded content added by the school may require additional cookies or tracking technologies to be enabled in order to function.
You have the right to decide whether to accept or reject cookies. Be aware that cookie preferences are set on a per device basis; therefore you may need to set your preferences on each device you use.
Initial cookie pop-up banner: You can exercise preferences about what cookies are served on our Websites by selecting your preference from this modal which appears upon visiting an eSchools website/login screen and dashboard. You can also change your cookie preferences by clicking on the link on the footer of any page. The banner will reappear annually (August 31st to coincide with the academic year) to confirm your settings.
Browser Controls: You can set or amend your web browser controls to accept or refuse cookies. If you choose to reject cookies, you may still use our Websites though your access to some functionality and areas of our Websites may be restricted. As the means by which you can refuse cookies through your web browser controls vary from browser-to-browser, you should visit your browser’s help menu for more information.
Disabling Most Interest Based Advertising: Most advertising networks offer you a way to opt out of Interest Based Advertising. We will not, without your express consent, supply your personal information to any third party for the purpose of their or any other third party's direct marketing.
